newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia farmers say meat reforms workable.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia farmers say meat reforms workable.

text.p: Reforms to Australia's meat industry statutory bodies announced by Primary Industries Minister John Anderson this week could work with further refinement, the New South Wales Farmers Association said on Wednesday.
But they would require co-operation from all industry sectors, Association president Ian Donges said in a statement.

The proposed structure outlined by Andersion was framed against the background of phasing out the roles of existing statutory meat industry bodies and increased roles for commercial enterprises and vertical alliances, he said.
"As such the structures ... foreshadowed are designed to be service-providers to the industry and not to lead the industry," Donges said.

It was understandable that a single body had been preferred to separate species-specific (cattle and sheep) bodies as in the longer term it would be expected that the role of this organisation would gradually contract, he said.
NSW Farmers preferred that promotion and marketing activities be carried out by subsidiary corporations rather than by separate operating units under one board, he said.
It was hoped the new organisation could have the flexibility to develop subsidiary companies if it preferred, he said.
Donges also expressed reservations about the proposed voluntary levy for the processing sector, saying he hoped processors could produce a suitable decision-making process.
Anderson announced on Tuesday that a single meat corporation with one board and separate operational units would replace the red meat industry's three existing main statutory authorities.
A producer owned and funded company will be established to replace the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp and the Meat Research Corp. The Meat Industry Council will be wound up.
